correctness.rationale: The sufficient-statistics reconstruction uses exact subtraction of adjacent ordered-pair counts from unrestricted pair counts; K,R,initial bit and unrestricted 01 count determine all four observed pair counts. For all n, their range supplies a fourth-degree upper bound. For n>=100 the explicit word family has positive integral exponents and exactly length n. The one-count and one-gap 11 count recover s,h; fixed s,h, the unrestricted 01 count is T0+8ma-(8m+1)d. Coprimality and bounded parameter differences force injectivity of a,d. This establishes the n^4 lower bound for every n>=100 without relying on finite enumeration. The standalone program independently verifies small profiles and witness sets; it is corroboration, not an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Contiguous 2-abelian equivalence records ordinary length-two factor multiplicities, while one-gap binomial equivalence records nonadjacent ordered pairs; they have different observables and different possible profile counts. The 2023 infinite-sequence results concern restricted factor languages and do not dominate the full binary shift case. Existing contiguous pair-spectrum code-size formulas likewise do not imply this gapped four-dimensional result.

value.rationale: The global growth rate of distinguishable gapped pair-deck outputs determines the maximal zero-error reconstruction codebook size and its sharp 4 log_2(n)+O(1)-bit information capacity. It is a natural full-language benchmark for a model whose existing literature focuses on collision thresholds or factors of restricted infinite words. Constructing four independently recoverable parameters with consecutive coprime coefficients supplies structural insight, not a routine special case or a table recomputation. No downstream paper-sized theorem is claimed; the logarithmic-capacity exponent is itself a meaningful natural invariant.
